The early Rattanakosin period saw the establishment of the new
Capital along with the revival of the country, both of which were labor- ;
intensive undertakings. Given labor shortage within the Thai community, p
the state had to recruit from among the Chinese to work in areas such as #
construction, canal digging and junk trade with China, which happened to
be the area where the country’s main source of revenue was generated. az
To encourage the Chinese, who were known for their unrivaled endurance a
and diligence and also adept in trade, to find jobs in Thailand, the † BI
government imposed numerous sets of attractive measures. FL
SS \t was during this period that the Chinese were the only people %8
entitled to freely enter and exit Thailand. Upon arrival, they could either Fe GFE
opt to obtain a tattoo mark on the wrist which Signified to which Officials
they belonged, just like Thai citizens, or live freely in exchange for
. payment of a certain government tax called in Thai “ohuk pi” Through it,
they enjoyed the Privilege of seeking employment anywhere in the
country, instead of being subject to the annual compulsory work
recruitment as an official’s vassals lasting three to four months the way
> Thai citizens were. Thus, the Chinese were given a vast array of
opportunities to earn their living and attain Prosperity. Besides working as
\aborers, many became skilled technicians, traders, fruit and vegetable
‘ sàn poultry and pig raisers and, finally, millionaires.

Eski Türkiye'de dini değerlere ve mütedeyyin insanlara karşı e
var olan düşmanca tutum, insanların dini yaşamlarını özgürce o
yaşamasına engel oluyordu. 1970'li yıllarda Türkiye'nin bu o
durumundan yararlanıp insanların dini duygularını istismar eden
Fetullah Gülen ve etrafındakiler, Fetullahçı Terör Örgütü'nün o
(FETS) ilk kurumlarını açmaya başladılar.
FETÖ, katı bir hiyerarşinin olduğu, üyelerinin şifreli konuşmayı
ve gizli mesajlar vermeyi tercih ettiği bir yapılanmadır. Bu terör
örgütü üyeleri istihbarata, emniyete, yargı ve askeri yapılanmalara
gizli yollarla sızmaya başladılar. Herhangi bir kurumda yeterince
örgütlendiklerini düşündüklerinde ise bu sefer açıktan
kendilerinden olmayan diğer kurum çalışanlarını hedef aldılar.
Bu yolda şantaj kasetleri, iftiralar, sınav sorularının çalınması gibi
haksız ve hukuksuz yöntemleri kullandılar.
Dış dünyaya ve Türkiye'nin mütedeyyin insanlarına iyilik sever,
ılımlı ve yardımcı görünen FETÖ bu kisvesiyle uzun yıllar kendini
gizledi. Örgüt; dini kisve ile hareket etse de dini faaliyet adı altında
Fetullah Gülen'in konuşmalarını dinletmek, kitaplarını okutmak ve
bir kişilik kültü inşa etmekten ileri gitmedi. Örgüt üyelerinin çeşitli
yöntemlerle beynini yıkayan FETÖ belli bir süre sonra üyelerine
Fethullah Gülen'in mehdi olduğu imalarını yapmaya ve idari
görevlere getirdiği kişilere de bunu açıktan söylemeye başladı.
FETÖ her kurumda uyguladığı, sızıp belirli bir çoğunluğu
yakaladıktan sonra, kendisinden olmayanlara savaş açma taktiğini
en son devlete karşı uyguladı. Devletin farklı kademelerinde
örgütlendikten sonra yeterli çoğunluğa ulaştığını düşünen FETÖ,
17-25 Aralık ile başlayan süreçte, AK Parti hükümetine ve devlete
karşı savaş açtı. Bu savaşta her alanda yenilgiye uğrayan FETÖ,
15 Temmuz 2016 öncesi köşeye sıkıştığını anlayınca bu kez asker
içerisindeki mensubları ile darbe yapmaya kalkıştı. Silahsız
vatandaşlara otomatik silahlarla, tanklarla ve uçaklarla saldırıldığı
15 Temmuz gecesi, FETÖ'nün en kanlı eylemi olarak tarihe geçti.
FETÖ psikolojik savaş tekniklerini kullanarak, istihbarat ve |
lobicilik faaliyetlerine yurtiçi ve yurtdışında ağırlık veren bir terör
örgütüdür. Maşa olarak kullandığı diğer terör örgütleriyle birlikte
hareket ederek, gerek şiddet ve gerekse psikolojik savaş eylemleri
yapmış ve yaptırmıştır. FETÖ elebaşısı Fetullah Gülen halen

Naming ritual
For many ethnic communities naming the baby is an important
transition ritual through which the ancestors are notified of the
baby’s birth. The Yao believe that babies who đo not receive a
name can not join the ancestors when they die. Different hopes
for the child are signified in the family’s choice of name. The
Hanhi often use the father’s first name as a middle name for sons
as a proof of continual lineage. The Ede take the name of a
deceased person for their child in memory of their ancestors.
The Hmong avoid the name of deceased family members as the
child’s first name. Therefore when the dead are invoked the
newborn child’s name is not mentioned. Some Viet parents give a
temporary ‘ugly’ name to their child in the hope that evil spirits
will then not want the baby.

Pregnant women must respect special taboos and fulfil certain
rituals in order to protect themselves and the foetus. Viet
women present offerings at pagodas and temples and ask
monks for amulets to wear and place at their bedside in the
hope that the spirits will protect them. In some ethnic groups a
shaman is invited to perform a ritual in the home for good
health and an easy delivery for the pregnant woman. The Ede
organize a ritual for good health in the 7th month of pregnancy.
The ritual master banishes evil and asks for good health for the
woman and her foetus. The family provide alcohol and meat for
their quests.

Delivery and placenta
Before the 1960s many women in ethnic minority communities
gave birth at home in the yard or under a temporary shelter in the
forest depending on the ethnic group. Traditionally women gave
birth in standing, squatting or kneeling positions. To facilitate
childbirth the Viet drink sesame seed soup. When a problem arises
for a pregnant Hmong or Yao woman, the family invites a ritual
master to conduct rituals. The Thai apply sesame paste to the
stomachs of pregnant women. Traditionally the Hmong bury the
placenta at the foot of the principal column in the house. The Ede
place the placenta in a calabash that is then buried at the edge
of a spring. Other populations hang the placenta in a forest tree.
Today childbirth usually occurs at a clinic although the umbilical
cord is often cut at home.

This is Le Thi Xung’s second notebook, started on her 20th birthday, July 11th 1968. Enrolled in the popular militia in 1966,
she was in charge of liaison work and guarding the hamlet. The daily lives of the villagers of Vinh Giang in particular, and of
the district of Vinh Linh in general are recorded in the three notebooks of her private diary.
The 315 - page notebook, details her daily life and that of the inhabitants of Vinh Giang during 1968. It was the hardest year
of the war. “On the 18th of October 1968, after a sustained gunfire attack, the enemy attacked suddenly again. ljust let the
fire in the kitchen go out, | did not have the time to look for my purse, the jet plane was behind me. With my comrades I left
for the front. When we came back, the huts and the trenches had disappeared, gun fire stopped in the middle of the trench.”
The notebook ended on February 1st 1971, a few months before Xung s wedding. She wrote of her feelings and emotions just
before the return of her fiancé after six years of separation. The last lines of this diary were written by the fiancé, expressing his
feelings after he had read what she had written about him.

mobilized and displaced abroad. This is 8 space of consolation for
those victims whose remains were forever lost and never returned
home, and a space of remembrance for the bereaved families.

help the audience remember the history of forced mobilization and
the pains of war while reflecting on the significance of peace and
human rights.
We ask that visitors honor those enshrined with a solemn and
respectful demeanor.
